algo-001.base: What do you do if the residuals show a pattern?
variants: The residual plot shows a clear U shape. What does that tell you, and what do you change?
Residuals look fine overall but are much larger for one customer segment. What would you try?
Three data points with extreme values pull your fitted line noticeably. How do you handle them?
Why does least squares give outliers so much influence compared with absolute error?

algo-001.base: What changes if you care about inference instead of prediction?
variants: Your stakeholder now wants to know how much price affects demand, not just to predict demand. Which assumptions suddenly matter more?
Two features are highly correlated. Does that hurt prediction, inference or both?

algo-002.base: Why does lasso set some coefficients exactly to zero while ridge does not?
variants: Draw the constraint regions for L1 and L2 penalties. Why does the L1 region produce zeros?
Ridge shrinks a coefficient from 3.0 to 0.1 but never to zero. Why?

algo-002.base: What happens with a group of highly correlated features?
variants: Five features measure nearly the same thing. What does lasso do with them, and what does elastic net do?
Your lasso model picks a different feature from a correlated group each time you resample the data. What would you change?

algo-002.base: How do you choose the penalty strength?
variants: How would you pick the lambda for ridge, and why must the features be scaled first?
Cross-validation gives a range of penalties with similar error. Which do you choose, and why?

algo-003.base: What is impurity and how is it measured?
variants: A node has 80 of one class and 20 of the other. Compute its Gini impurity, and explain what a split is trying to do to it.
Do Gini and entropy usually lead to different trees? Why or why not?

algo-003.base: How can you stop a tree from overfitting?
variants: Your tree has 2,000 leaves, many with a single sample. Which settings would you change?
What is cost-complexity pruning, and how do you choose its strength?

algo-003.base: Can a tree predict beyond the range of its training data?
variants: Your training data has house sizes up to 300 square meters. What does a tree predict for a 500-square-meter house?
Why are tree-based models a poor choice for extrapolating a trend into the future?
How does a random forest estimate its error without a separate validation set?
When can out-of-bag error be misleading?

algo-004.base: Why are impurity-based importances biased toward some features?
variants: A random ID-like feature with many unique values ranks high in impurity importance. Why?
Why do continuous features tend to look more important than binary ones in impurity importance?
How does permutation importance work, and what goes wrong with correlated features?
When would you use SHAP values instead of permutation importance?

algo-005.base: How do their tree-growing strategies differ?
variants: LightGBM grows trees leaf-wise and XGBoost level-wise by default. What does that mean for overfitting on a small dataset?
Which parameter limits LightGBM's leaf-wise growth, and why does it matter?

algo-005.base: How does each handle categorical variables?
variants: You have a categorical feature with 5,000 levels. How would each of the three libraries handle it?
Why does CatBoost's ordered target statistics approach reduce target leakage?

algo-005.base: How would you compare them fairly?
variants: One library wins by 0.002 AUC but takes five times longer to train. How do you decide?
How do you make sure each library gets an equal tuning budget?

algo-006.base: What does the kernel trick do?
variants: The two classes form concentric circles. How can an SVM separate them?
What does an RBF kernel measure between two points?

algo-006.base: What do C and gamma control?
variants: You raise C and training accuracy rises while validation accuracy falls. What's happening?
What happens to the decision boundary as gamma gets very large?

algo-006.base: Why does an SVM scale poorly to millions of rows?
variants: Training an RBF SVM on 2 million rows hasn't finished after a day. Why, and what alternatives do you have?
When would a linear SVM still be practical at large scale?
Explain in plain words what the epsilon tube means for errors smaller than epsilon.
How does the choice of epsilon change the model?

algo-007.base: What happens to points inside the tube?
variants: Why does SVR end up depending on only some of the training points?
If you make epsilon larger, what happens to the number of support vectors?

algo-007.base: How does it compare with ridge for a typical tabular problem?
variants: Your dataset has 50 features and 100,000 rows. Would you try SVR or ridge first?
When might SVR's robustness to small errors be a real advantage?
With k = 1, training accuracy is 100%. Why is that not reassuring?
How does increasing k change bias and variance?

algo-008.base: Why does it struggle in high dimensions?
variants: With 300 features, why do all points end up roughly the same distance apart?
How would you make k-NN usable on high-dimensional data?
One feature is income in dollars and another is age in years. What happens to k-NN if you don't scale?
Would you use standardization or min-max scaling for k-NN, and why?
You include the same word feature twice. What does naive Bayes do with that?
Naive Bayes ranks spam well but its probabilities are near 0 or 1. Why?
A word never appeared in spam during training. What happens when it shows up in a new spam email without smoothing?
How does Laplace smoothing fix the zero-count problem?
How do you represent an email as features for multinomial naive Bayes?
When would you choose naive Bayes over logistic regression for text classification?

algo-010.base: What does a coefficient of 0.7 mean?
variants: The coefficient on 'number of late payments' is 0.7. By how much do the odds of default change for each extra late payment?
How would you explain a negative coefficient on income to a credit officer?

algo-010.base: What do you need to check about the features?
variants: Two features are strongly correlated and their coefficients have unexpected signs. What do you check?
Why should you scale features if you plan to regularize the logistic regression?

algo-010.base: How do you capture non-linear effects?
variants: Default risk rises sharply for very young and very old borrowers. How would you capture that in a logistic regression?
When would you bin a continuous feature, and what do you lose?

algo-011.base: How does an isolation forest decide a point is unusual?
variants: Why does an unusual transaction tend to be isolated with fewer random splits?
What does the anomaly score of an isolation forest actually measure?

algo-011.base: How do you set the alert threshold without labels?
variants: Analysts can review 200 transactions a day. How do you set the threshold?
How would you estimate precision when you only have analyst reviews of flagged cases?

algo-011.base: How do you know it finds fraud and not just unusual-but-fine transactions?
variants: The model flags many large but legitimate corporate purchases. How do you reduce that?
How would you use analyst feedback to improve the system over time?
Why might a linear model predict a negative number of claims, and what does a Poisson model do instead?
What does a Poisson regression assume about the mean and variance of claims?

algo-012.base: What do you do when the variance is much larger than the mean?
variants: Most customers have zero claims and a few have many. Which models would you consider?
How do you test whether a Poisson model is overdispersed?

algo-012.base: How do you handle customers observed for different lengths of time?
variants: Some customers were insured for three months, others for a full year. How do you account for that?
What is an offset in a Poisson regression, and why use the log of exposure?

algo-013.base: Why does the result depend on initialization?
variants: You run k-means five times and get five different results. Why, and how do you get a stable answer?
What does k-means++ do differently when choosing starting centroids?

algo-013.base: What kinds of cluster shapes does it handle poorly?
variants: Your data has one large cluster and two small ones. How does k-means handle that?
Why does k-means struggle with elongated or crescent-shaped clusters?

algo-013.base: Do you need to scale the features?
variants: One feature is annual spend in dollars and another is number of visits. What happens without scaling?
After scaling, a feature you consider minor now influences the clusters as much as spend. Is that a problem?

algo-014.base: What do eps and min_samples control?
variants: You increase eps. What happens to the number of clusters and noise points?
How would you choose eps using a k-distance plot?

algo-014.base: How does DBSCAN treat noise points?
variants: DBSCAN labels 30% of your points as noise. Is that a problem?
How is DBSCAN's treatment of outliers different from k-means'?
Your data has one dense cluster and one sparse cluster. Can a single eps capture both?
Why does DBSCAN become hard to tune with many features?

algo-015.base: What is the difference between single, complete and average linkage?
variants: Single linkage gives you one huge cluster that snakes through the data. Why?
When would you choose Ward's linkage?

algo-015.base: How do you decide where to cut the tree?
variants: The dendrogram shows a large jump in merge height between 4 and 3 clusters. What does that suggest?
The business wants exactly five segments, but the dendrogram suggests three. What do you do?

algo-015.base: Why is it hard to run on a million points?
variants: Why does agglomerative clustering need memory that grows with the square of the number of points?
How could you cluster a million customers hierarchically in practice?

algo-016.base: How is a mixture model fitted?
variants: Describe in plain words what the E step and the M step do.
Why can a mixture model get stuck in a poor solution, and what do you do about it?

algo-016.base: What happens if you give the model too many components?
variants: How would you choose the number of components using BIC?
You fit 20 components to data with 3 real groups. What happens?

algo-016.base: When would you prefer k-means anyway?
variants: The clusters are roughly round and you have 10 million points. Would you use a mixture model?
When are soft assignments worth the extra complexity?

algo-017.base: What do silhouette scores tell you, and what don't they?
variants: Silhouette is highest at k = 2, but the business wants more detail. How much weight do you put on the silhouette?
Why can silhouette scores favor round, evenly sized clusters?
How would you check whether your clusters change if you resample the customers?
You rerun clustering on next month's data and the segments look different. What does that tell you?

algo-017.base: What is the business test of a segmentation?
variants: Marketing says two of your segments behave the same in campaigns. What does that say about the segmentation?
How would you test whether the segments lead to different results when targeted?

algo-018.base: How do you combine numeric and categorical features?
variants: You have age, income, account type and region. How do you compute distances between customers?
One-hot encoding region creates 50 binary columns. What does that do to a distance-based clustering?

algo-018.base: How would you make the segments explainable?
variants: The relationship managers ask what makes segment 3 different. How do you answer clearly?
How would a shallow decision tree help explain the segments?

algo-018.base: How often should segments be refreshed?
variants: Customers keep moving between segments each month. Is that a problem?
How would you refresh segments without confusing teams that use them?

algo-019.base: How do you decide how many components to keep?
variants: The first 10 components explain 85% of the variance, the first 50 explain 95%. How do you choose?
When would you choose the number of components by downstream model performance instead of variance explained?
A stakeholder asks what component 1 means. How do you answer?
The loadings of component 2 mix 30 features with similar weights. Can you interpret it?

algo-019.base: When is PCA a bad idea?
variants: Would you apply PCA before training a gradient-boosted model? Why or why not?
Your data lies on a curved surface. What will PCA miss?

algo-020.base: What do distances between clusters in a t-SNE plot mean?
variants: Two clusters are far apart in the t-SNE plot. Does that mean they're very different?
Can you compare cluster sizes in a t-SNE plot?

algo-020.base: How do perplexity and other settings change the picture?
variants: Changing perplexity from 30 to 5 turns three clusters into ten. What does that tell you?
Would you expect UMAP to show the same picture? Why might it differ?

algo-020.base: How would you check that the clusters are real?
variants: How would you test whether the clusters in the plot exist in the original data?
Random noise data can still produce clusters in t-SNE. How would you use that as a check?

algo-021.base: What is the difference between filter, wrapper and embedded methods?
variants: Give an example of a filter method and a wrapper method. Which would you run on 2,000 features?
How does lasso count as an embedded feature selection method?

algo-021.base: How can feature selection cause leakage?
variants: You pick the 50 features most correlated with the target on all 10,000 rows, then cross-validate. What's wrong?
How do you include feature selection inside cross-validation?

algo-021.base: When would you not bother selecting?
variants: You're using a gradient-boosted model. Do you need feature selection at all?
When would you still remove features even if accuracy doesn't change?

algo-022.base: Why must the second-level model be trained on out-of-fold predictions?
variants: You train the meta-model on predictions the base models made on their own training data. What happens?
How do you generate the out-of-fold predictions for stacking?

algo-022.base: How different do the base models need to be?
variants: You stack three gradient-boosted models with different seeds. Do you expect much gain? Why?
Which kinds of base models tend to combine well?

algo-022.base: What does it cost in production?
variants: The stacked model adds 0.3% AUC but needs four models in production. How do you decide?
What does stacking do to latency and debugging?

algo-023.base: Why can SMOTE hurt if applied before splitting the data?
variants: You apply SMOTE to the whole dataset and then cross-validate. Why are the scores too optimistic?
Where in the pipeline should SMOTE go?

algo-023.base: How does class imbalance change which metric you use?
variants: With 2% positives, a model gets 98% accuracy. Which metric would you report instead?
Why can ROC-AUC look good while precision at your chosen threshold is poor?

algo-023.base: Which approach would you try first, and why?
variants: Which would you try first: SMOTE, class weights or threshold tuning? Why?
Class weights improve recall but your probabilities are now too high. What happened?

algo-024.base: Why is random search often better than grid search?
variants: You have six hyperparameters but only two really matter. Why does random search find good values faster than grid search?

variants: How does Bayesian optimization choose the next set of hyperparameters to try?
